items.title: The Twelfth and Final Favourable Condition: Resting on the Four Absorptions

items.zh: 云何依三摩地？謂彼如是斷五蓋已，便能遠離心隨煩惱。遠離諸欲惡不善法，有尋有伺，離生喜樂；入初靜慮具足安住。尋伺寂靜，於內等淨，心一趣性，無尋無伺，定生喜樂；第二靜慮具足安住。遠離喜貪，安住捨、念及以正知，身領受樂；聖所宣說，捨、念具足安樂而住；第三靜慮具足安住。究竟斷樂，先斷於苦，喜憂俱沒，不苦不樂，捨念清淨；第四靜慮具足安住。如是名為依三摩地。
items.en: What is resting on concentration? It is that, having cut off the five hindrances in this way, one is able to become free of the secondary afflictions that follow the mind. Secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unwholesome states, [one enters], with directed thought and sustained thought, the joy and ease born of seclusion: one abides, fully accomplished, in the first absorption. With directed and sustained thought stilled, with inner equanimity and clarity and one-pointedness of mind, free of directed and sustained thought, [one enters] the joy and ease born of concentration: one abides, fully accomplished, in the second absorption. Free of attachment to joy, abiding in equanimity, mindfulness, and clear awareness, experiencing ease in the body [in fact, through the mind] — that state the noble ones describe as "dwelling in equanimity, mindfulness, and ease" — one abides, fully accomplished, in the third absorption. With ease finally abandoned, having earlier abandoned discomfort, joy and displeasure both having vanished, [one enters] the neither-painful-nor-pleasant state of purified equanimity and mindfulness: one abides, fully accomplished, in the fourth absorption. This is called resting on concentration.

items.title: Section: The Twelve Favourable Conditions Complete — Establishment Itself Closes

items.zh: 彼由如是漸次修行，後後轉勝、轉增、轉上，修集諸緣，初自圓滿，依三摩地以為最後。得如是心清淨鮮白，無諸瑕穢，離隨煩惱，質直堪能，安住無動。若復獲得依四聖諦，為令遍知、永斷、作證、修習他音教授教誡；便有如是堪能勢力，發生如理所引作意，及彼為先所有正見。由此便能於四聖諦入真現觀，圓滿解脫，於無餘依般涅槃界而般涅槃。當知此中始從正見，圓滿解脫，於無餘依般涅槃界而般涅槃，是名種性真實修集。從自圓滿，乃至最後依三摩地，當知是名修集劣緣。若依四諦法教增上所有教授教誡他音，若如正理所引作意，當知是名修集勝緣。如是名為種[＊]性安立。
items.en: Through this gradual practice, becoming progressively more excellent, more developed, and more elevated, one cultivates these conditions — beginning with one's own perfection, and ending, finally, with resting on concentration. …By this means, one is thereby able to enter the direct realisation of the four noble truths, achieving complete liberation, and, within the realm of nirvāṇa without residue, attains final nirvāṇa. It should be understood that all of this — beginning from correct view, through complete liberation, to attaining final nirvāṇa within the realm of nirvāṇa without residue — is called the genuine cultivation of lineage. From one's own perfection up through the last, resting on concentration, this should be understood as the cultivation of the lesser conditions. Relying on the excellent sound of instruction and admonition centred on the teaching of the four noble truths, together with the attention drawn forth by correct principle — this should be understood as the cultivation of the superior condition. This is called the establishment of spiritual lineage.

items.title: Section: The Marks of One Who Abides in Lineage Open

items.zh: 云何住種[＊]性者所有諸相？謂與一切無涅槃法補特伽羅諸相相違，當知即名安住種[＊]性補特伽羅所有諸相。問：何等名為無涅槃法補特伽羅所有諸相，成就彼故，應知說名無涅槃法補特伽羅？
items.en: What are the marks possessed by one who abides in lineage? Whatever is contrary to all the marks of a person who lacks the dharma of nirvāṇa — this should be understood as precisely the marks possessed by a person who abides in lineage. Question: What are the marks possessed by a person who lacks the dharma of nirvāṇa, such that, upon possessing them, that person should be understood to be called a person who lacks the dharma of nirvāṇa?

items.title: The First Two Marks of No Lineage: A Self-Love No Buddha Can Break, and Indifference to Both Saṃsāra and Nirvāṇa

items.zh: 答：無涅槃法補特伽羅有眾多相，我今當說彼相少分。謂彼最初不住種[＊]性無涅槃法補特伽羅，阿賴耶愛，遍一切種皆悉隨縛，附屬所依，成無量法不可傾拔，久遠隨逐，畢竟堅固，依附相續，一切諸佛所不能救。是名第一不住種[＊]性補特伽羅無種姓相。復有所餘不住種姓補特伽羅無種姓相。謂彼聽聞以無量門呵毀生死眾多過失，又復聽聞以無量門稱讚涅槃眾多功德，而於生死不見少分戲論過失，不見少分所有過患，亦復不能少分厭離。如是見厭，於過去世不能已生；於未來世不能當生；於現在世不能正生。又於愛盡寂滅涅槃，不見少分下劣功德，不見少分所有勝利，亦復不能少分欣樂。如是見樂，於過去世不能已生；於未來世不能當生；於現在世不能正生。是名第二不住種姓補特伽羅無種姓相。復有所餘不住種姓補特伽羅無種姓相。
items.en: Answer: A person who lacks the dharma of nirvāṇa has many marks; I shall now describe a portion of them. The first mark of a person who does not abide in lineage, who lacks the dharma of nirvāṇa, is this: attachment to the storehouse consciousness, binding every kind of experience without exception, attached to its underlying basis, forming countless states that cannot be dislodged, following that person across a vast span of time, ultimately unshakeable, adhering and continuing without break — such that not even any buddha is able to rescue that person from it. This is called the first mark of a person who does not abide in lineage. …Such a person, though hearing saṃsāra's many faults condemned through countless approaches, and though hearing nirvāṇa's many virtues praised through countless approaches, sees not the slightest fault of conceptual proliferation in saṃsāra, not the slightest danger, nor is able to feel even the slightest revulsion towards it. …And regarding nirvāṇa — the quiescence of exhausted craving — that person sees not the slightest inferior virtue in it, nor the slightest excellent benefit, nor is able to feel even the slightest joy towards it. …This is called the second mark of a person who does not abide in lineage.

items.title: Marks Three and Four: Shameless Delight in Wrongdoing, and a Heart Unmoved by the Dharma

items.zh: 謂彼本性成就上品無慚無愧。由是因緣，無有厭惡，心無怯畏。以歡喜心現行眾惡。由是因緣，未甞追悔。唯觀現法。由是因緣，自身財寶衰退過患。是名第三不住種姓補特伽羅無種姓相。復有所餘不住種姓補特伽羅無種姓相。謂一切種圓滿分明稱當道理，美妙、殊勝、易可解了。或依苦諦、或依集諦、或依滅諦、或依道諦宣說開示正法教時，不能獲得微小發心，微小信解，況能獲得身毛為竪、悲泣墮淚？如是亦依過去、未來、現在世別。是名第四不住種姓補特伽羅無種姓相。復有所餘不住種姓補特伽羅無種姓相。
items.en: Such a person, by nature, has fully developed the highest degree of shamelessness — no sense of shame before oneself, and no sense of shame before others. Because of this, that person feels no self-disgust, and the mind knows no timidity. Wrongdoing of every kind is carried out with a joyful mind. Because of this, no regret is ever felt afterwards. Only the present life is ever considered — and because of this, there is the danger that one's own wealth and resources will decline. This is called the third mark. …[The Dharma may be taught] in every possible way complete, lucid, perfectly in accord with reason, beautifully expressed, excellent [free of any self-seeking], and easy to understand. …Yet whether it is taught resting on the truth of suffering, its origin, its cessation, or the path, that person is unable to give rise to even the slightest resolve, the slightest confidence — let alone have the hairs of the body stand on end, or weep tears. This holds true across the past, the future, and the present alike. This is called the fourth mark.

blocks.text: The twelve conditions conclude with the four absorptions. Then the treatise describes the marks of one who abides in lineage, and, at length, the marks of one who does not.

"Having cut off the five hindrances, one is free of the mind's secondary afflictions", and abides in the four absorptions. Venerable Miào Jìng: in those who do not practise, "the mind moves along with affliction"; here the mind no longer follows it. In the third absorption, "equanimity" is the 捨 of the four immeasurables. "Experiencing ease in the body" is really the mind, since the sense consciousnesses are not operating.
From right view through complete liberation to final nirvāṇa is the genuine cultivation of lineage; from one's own perfection to resting on concentration are its conditions.

subs.head: Marks of lineage and no lineage

blocks.text: The marks of lineage are simply the contrary of the marks of one without it. The treatise gives six marks of the latter, "only a small portion" (Master Cháng Bǎi). 1. **Attachment to the ālayavijñāna** "binding every kind of experience, unshakeable": a self-love no Buddha can break. Venerable Miào Jìng: all beings have this attachment; for these it is beyond loosening. 2. **No sense of danger in saṃsāra, no sense of merit in nirvāṇa**, even on hearing them taught. 3. **Shamelessness**: "wrongdoing of every kind is carried out with a joyful mind." Master Cháng Bǎi: shame (慚) is before oneself, embarrassment (愧) before others. 4. **A heart unmoved by the Dharma**: hearing even the most excellent teaching, given without any ulterior motive, one feels nothing.
These marks describe extremes. In practice almost everyone shows some of them some of the time. The teachers both stress that this is not a tool for judging others.

quiz.q: What is the twelfth condition, "resting on concentration"?
options: having cut the five hindrances and freed from the mind's secondary afflictions, abiding in the four absorptions
quiz.why: "Having cut off the five hindrances in this way, one is able to become free of the mind's secondary afflictions," then abides in the four absorptions. Venerable Miào Jìng: this amounts to cultivating insight within concentration, not outside it.

quiz.q: How do the masters explain "inner equanimity and purity" (於內等淨) in the second absorption?
options: Miào Jìng: 等 means equanimity; Cháng Bǎi: it is the counteracting factor against the disturbance of examination and analysis
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: this 等 means equanimity, as in the 捨 of the four immeasurables. Master Cháng Bǎi: among the four factors of the second absorption, inner purity is the counteracting factor against the disturbance of examination and analysis. The English "inner clarity" misses the sense of equanimity.

quiz.q: In the third absorption, "experiencing ease in the body" — the English and note take it as bodily. What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: it is really the mind, since the five sense consciousnesses do not operate then
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "experiencing ease in the body" is really the mind, because at this point the five sense consciousnesses do not operate, so there is no question of body consciousness.

quiz.q: What does the treatise call the genuine cultivation of lineage, the cultivation of lesser conditions, and of superior conditions?
options: from right view through liberation to final nirvāṇa is genuine cultivation; from one's own perfection to concentration, lesser conditions; instruction on the four truths and correct attention, superior conditions
quiz.why: From right view through complete liberation to final nirvāṇa is the genuine cultivation of lineage; from one's own perfection up to resting on concentration, the cultivation of lesser conditions; instruction on the four truths and properly guided attention, the cultivation of superior conditions. Master Cháng Bǎi: only uncontaminated supramundane right view is the genuine cultivation of lineage.

quiz.q: The treatise says those lacking nirvāṇa "have many marks; I shall describe a portion." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: not all — only a small portion, in six kinds
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: it does not reveal all of them, only a small portion, divided into six kinds.

quiz.q: What is the first mark of one without lineage?
options: attachment to the storehouse consciousness binding everything, immovable, utterly firm — no buddha can rescue them
quiz.why: "Attachment to the storehouse consciousness, binding every kind of experience… forming countless states that cannot be dislodged… ultimately unshakeable… such that not even any buddha is able to rescue that person." Master Cháng Bǎi: the seventh consciousness clings to the eighth's seeing-part as self, loving the self intensely.

quiz.q: How do the two masters distinguish 慚 and 愧?
options: 慚 concerns oneself, 愧 concerns others
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 慚 is shame before oneself, 愧 before others; one who cannot respect oneself has no 慚. Venerable Miào Jìng: regarding oneself it is "no 慚," regarding others "no 愧."
